questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Namibia about 825,615 square kilometres; South Sudan about 644,329 square kilometres; Central African Republic about 622,984 square kilometres; São Tomé and Príncipe about 1,001 square kilometres.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Namibia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Namibia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Windhoek?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Namibia is Windhoek.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Namibia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Namibia article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Namibia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Namibia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Namibia article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by the countries of Angola and Zambia to the north, Botswana to the east, and South Africa to the south.
